body: Would be nice to have generics here, but we can improve that later.
You can avoid the cast with `querySelector<HTMLElement>` inside the function.
We test two times that options without `container` throws an error.
Do we really have to trigger this on each render?
Why this type is useful? We can directly provide `QueryRuleCustomDataWidgetParams` to the renderer.
We have to investigate why we have to cast here, but definitely not a blocker.

Actually I think the `prepareTemplateProps` already do [the merge of the `templates`](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/60a965df3443d14759657e282172cf3440621cdd/src/lib/utils/prepareTemplateProps.ts#L16-L18).
The name does not seem to match the widget.

Actually we have no guarantee of the type safety here. The widget should accept a generic type that would be pass to `transformItems`. Then the data provided to the template could be inferred from the return of type for `transformItems`. I'm not saying that it's easy though, we can improve it later.
Nope, because at the renderer level `container` _must_ be an `HTMLElement`, and not `string | HTMLElement`.

In this case it's because `container` is required in `QueryRuleCustomDataWidgetParams`.

Since we want to keep the pattern of `const widget = (options = {})` and `container` doesn't exist in `{}`, it's necessary to cast `{}` to `QueryRuleCustomDataWidgetParams`. Does that make sense?
Indeed, I'll simplify this. I wonder if we still need `prepareTemplateProps` actually. Thoughts?
Good catch – that's a remaining of my POC.
Exactly – that's a discussion that we've had already.

Then the signature becomes:

```js
getContainerNode(selectorOrHTMLElement: string | HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null
```

While we don't want (and it can't) be `null`.
With a proper typing of `isDOMElement` we should not have the issue, we can ensure that at this stage the selector is a DOM element.
Yes indeed, a different name would have helped to understand IMO. The `container` has nothing to do with the connector it's only used for the rendering. It's confusing to see it in the name.
Yes.
We can keep it for now and see what is the impact of change. It does add some information on the object like `useCustomCompileOptions`. Not sure why it's useful though.

I removed `prepareTemplateProps` in the last change.

> Not sure why it's useful though.

Exactly my thought too.
I renamed it `QueryRuleCustomDataRendererWidgetParams`.

Yep, looks like `isDomElement` should be a type guard: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/advanced-types.html#type-guards-and-differentiating-types

(and the post by @wittydeveloper [medium](https://medium.com/@wittydeveloper/typescript-make-types-real-the-type-guard-functions-814364e8dbe3))
Indeed, that's what we're looking for!

I don't think the `window` is really useful in that case. We can simplify the condition and remove the `@ts-ignore`. Note that the rest of the condition does not entirely satisfy the type constraint. `nodeType` greater than 0 can represent `Element`, `Text`, `Comment`, ... Which is incompatible with our type but anyway it's working.
Indeed – I didn't want to change this condition in a minor because some users probably rely on this check.

I think React/Preact throw an error if the container is not an `Element`. It means that `Text`, `Comment` should not be taken into account for the check.

![Screenshot 2019-03-22 at 13 03 35](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6513513/54821584-ec09f800-4ca2-11e9-9857-656bb12eaaf5.png)
I checked online the other day and apparently the second check is for browsers not supporting `window.HTMLElement`. We can still change these checks on another iteration.
